t: You're at the Charterhouse, a historic complex of buildings in Clerkenwell, dating from the fourteenth century. It began in 1371 as a Carthusian priory, on the site of a Black Death burial ground. Walter de Manny, the soldier who founded it, is buried here. After the priory was dissolved in 1537, it was rebuilt as a great Tudor courtyard house. In 1611 Thomas Sutton bought it and set up a school and an almshouse. The almshouse is still lived in today. Several people died here, including the theologian Thomas Burnet, the painter Adrian Daintrey and the engraver Joseph Skelton.
